title: Credential-schema evolution and semantic-downgrade boundary
hypothesis: A structural schema-evolution profile can reject a synthetic credential whose version transition removes required meaning, redefines protected terms, or silently accepts an older interpretation without claiming cryptographic or production assurance.
null_or_failure: A required claim disappears, a protected term changes meaning, an unknown critical field is ignored, a context version floats, downgrade is silent, canonicalization changes semantic identity, or structural acceptance becomes a real-key, live-resolution, privacy, interoperability, or production claim.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Exercise additive optional fields, missing required fields, protected-term redefinition, unknown critical fields, floating contexts, explicit and silent downgrade, canonicalization divergence, and production-promotion fixtures; require unsafe evolution to fail closed.
rollback_or_recovery: Reject the evolved credential, retain the vector, restore the last explicitly supported schema and context pin, and require standards-conformant real keys and proofs, live resolution and status, interoperability, privacy assurance, independent security review, and trust governance before production use.
boundary: Synthetic schema checks do not supply real keys, proofs, live resolution or status, interoperability, privacy review, security review, or governance.
